title: Purple Giraffe
cn: 第 2 集 · 紫色长颈鹿
novel:
Ted had one problem: he wanted to see Robin again, but he needed an [[excuse|excuse]].

So he decided to [[throw a party|throw a party]] and pretend it was a [[casual|casual]] idea. He hung an [[inflatable|inflatable]] purple giraffe over the sofa and wrote a crooked [[banner|banner]]. Robin promised to [[show up|show up]].

She did not.

So he threw the same party again. And again. By the third weekend the flat smelled of [[stale|stale]] beer, there were [[stacks|stack]] of dirty cups on every table, and the fridge was full of sad [[leftovers|leftover]]. Marshall said the word "[[persistent|persistent]]" politely; Lily said the word "[[stubborn|stubborn]]" honestly; Barney said it was simply [[humiliating|humiliating]].

Ted did not care. He was [[clinging to|cling to]] one thought like a man in cold water, and he refused to [[give up on|give up on]] it.

On the fourth night, [[worn out|worn out]] and completely [[sober|sober]], he sat alone under the [[dim|dim]] kitchen light and finally decided to let his little [[crush|crush]] die.

Then the door opened. Robin stood there, laughing at the giraffe.

"What a [[coincidence|coincidence]]," Ted lied. [[Eventually|eventually]] he told her the truth: there had been four parties, and all of them were for her.

excuse.en: a reason you give so that people do not know your real reason

throw a party.en: to organise a party at your home

casual.en: relaxed, not planned and not serious

inflatable.en: that you fill with air to make it big

banner.en: a long piece of cloth or paper with words on it

show up.en: to arrive at a place where people are waiting for you

stale.en: old and no longer fresh or nice

stack.en: a pile of things put one on top of another

leftover.en: food that was not eaten and is kept for later

persistent.en: continuing to try, again and again

stubborn.en: refusing to change your mind, even when you are wrong

humiliating.en: making you feel very ashamed in front of other people

cling to.en: to hold something very tightly and not let it go

give up on.en: to stop hoping that something or someone will work

dim.en: not bright; with only a little light

crush.en: a strong but short feeling of love for someone

coincidence.en: when two things happen at the same time by luck, not by plan

eventually.en: in the end, after a long time
